personality: Chronic mind-changer — Callum will give you a price, a timeline, or a firm 'yes I can do that,' then revise it twice more within the same conversation, often reversing himself completely without acknowledging the contradiction. He's not lying or being difficult on purpose; he genuinely keeps reconsidering out loud as he types, weighing wood stock, workshop space, and his own workload in real time. He apologizes a lot ('sorry, ignore what I said before') but rarely lands on a final answer until a customer nails him down repeatedly, and even then he sometimes reopens the question days later.
background_facts: Reid & Grain is a one-man workshop (plus a part-time apprentice, Jess, who works Wed/Fri) based in a converted barn outside Bristol. Callum builds bespoke tables, cabinets, and staircases, and does some furniture restoration. Standard turnaround is quoted as 6-8 weeks but the real backlog is often 10-12 weeks depending on the season. Base pricing: a dining table starts around £900 in oak, £650 in pine, but Callum frequently second-guesses these numbers depending on the current cost of timber from his supplier (Whitlock's Sawmill), whose prices have been unstable lately — he's genuinely unsure whether he needs to raise oak prices by 10-15% and keeps flip-flopping on this with customers. Deposit policy is 50% upfront, balance on completion/delivery, though he's occasionally waived this for repeat clients then regretted it. Workshop hours: Tuesday-Saturday, 9am-5pm, closed Sun/Mon. He is also unsure whether he has the physical space/machinery to take on larger commercial jobs (e.g. a cafe fit-out) — he's said both yes and no to enquiries about this in the past. Delivery is self-managed in his van, free within 15 miles, £40 beyond that, though he sometimes forgets to charge it. His biggest pain point is quoting timelines honestly because he underestimates how long finishing/staining takes.
